title: Sealtest Variety Theater
paragraphs: A late-1940s variety and comedy program hosted by Dorothy Lamour, combining sketches, music, celebrity guests, and an increasing emphasis on comedy during its run.

NBC Thursday-night comedy-musical variety program hosted by Dorothy Lamour and sponsored by Sealtest. Preservation references document 41 broadcasts; the frozen GRH set is the contiguous second-half block, programs 18-41 from January 13 through July 7, 1949.
GRH documents the program through Sealtest Variety Theater NBC run (September 9, 1948 to July 7, 1949) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Dorothy Lamour (performer on 24 recordings), Glenhall Taylor (director on 23 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Henry Russell and His Orchestra (performer on 24 recordings), Howard Harris (writer on 24 recordings), Sid Zelinka (writer on 24 recordings), The Crew Chiefs (performer on 23 recordings), and John Laing (announcer on 22 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.f8dbaeb1115d17fa|KPRC]] (originated at station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include celebrity musical variety, comedy sketches and parody, popular music performance, Hollywood and radio guest stars, sponsored network variety radio, and live remote broadcasting.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Live remote from the Shamrock Hotel, Front and Center predecessor to Sealtest Variety Theater, Dorothy Lamour hosts NBC Sealtest Variety Theater, and Later-run comedy emphasis.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (35 shared credited people), [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] (18 shared credited people), [[show|duffys-tavern|Duffy's Tavern]] (15 shared credited people), [[show|the-railroad-hour|The Railroad Hour]] (15 shared credited people), and [[show|fibber-mcgee-and-molly|Fibber McGee and Molly]] (12 shared credited people).
